components.title: Site certificate issuing
components.description: cert-manager issuing site certificates from the site PKI.

control-implementations.description: What the site stack's rendered manifests show about certificate issuers.

implemented-requirements.description: The site stack renders no certificate issuer that uses ACME.

statements.description: No Issuer or ClusterIssuer in the site stack's releases, rendered offline from the hash-checked vendored charts with the CI site file, has an ACME configuration; the Let's Encrypt issuer that the Theia Cloud base chart can render is switched off, and the render test fails if any rendered issuer names ACME.
statements.remarks: Your organization supplies the certificate authority that issues the site's certificates.

implemented-requirements.description: Site certificates come from the OpenBao intermediate.

statements.description: Every certificate the site stack renders is issued by site-pki or site-pki-hub, two cluster issuers of the vault type that sign only through OpenBao's pki_int roles, so the intermediate's key stays in OpenBao; the only other issuer, the bootstrap CA, issues OpenBao's first certificate only, which site-pki re-issues. No rendered issuer is ACME or self-signed, only the cert-manager controller may request the issuer account's token, and cert-manager's OpenBao policy allows only the two sign paths.
statements.remarks: Your organization's key custodians hold the site's root and sign its intermediate.

control-implementations.description: Supply-chain statements generated from the component inventory. Do not edit by hand: run node compliance/src/cli.ts supply-chain-statements --write.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the component inventory lists its resources.

statements.description: The component inventory (compliance/resources.json) lists these resources for Site certificate issuing, each with the pin the repository uses: image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-controller v1.21.3@sha256:9b262e9493ab3e0daebc2c9cfbddc6df68b9ac91afc036a759584f3d49d607e5, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-webhook v1.21.3@sha256:fc2845cc042ab57c8b98c5ff62462d50dcd5d8d3302f9e6875cd05042ce1020b, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-cainjector v1.21.3@sha256:165691f631d61931a27e4fbbb82bbed8205431d0446b3c14d170081aeff75f0a, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-startupapicheck v1.21.3@sha256:6b9e17adc075c80c0c5cb1f901654f0efa4c5d4b1a8b369985ac67f5bbb0b8d2 and chart cert-manager v1.21.3 (sha256:9ec67938b2981d8b333af61b3fcf53e26b4f6f5deb7ccda3de4ea116bb373a17). The compliance fit check over the whole repository, run as a CI test, fails when a resource the repository uses has no reviewed entry, or an entry lists a file that no longer uses it.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the inventory of what it installs at its site, with its owners, and reconciles it with this list.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the offline bundle import refuses a changed item.

statements.description: Before anything is copied to the site, the offline bundle import checks every item against the manifest your organization signed and refuses the bundle when an item is missing, extra or has another digest. For Site certificate issuing that covers image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-controller v1.21.3@sha256:9b262e9493ab3e0daebc2c9cfbddc6df68b9ac91afc036a759584f3d49d607e5, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-webhook v1.21.3@sha256:fc2845cc042ab57c8b98c5ff62462d50dcd5d8d3302f9e6875cd05042ce1020b, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-cainjector v1.21.3@sha256:165691f631d61931a27e4fbbb82bbed8205431d0446b3c14d170081aeff75f0a, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-startupapicheck v1.21.3@sha256:6b9e17adc075c80c0c5cb1f901654f0efa4c5d4b1a8b369985ac67f5bbb0b8d2 and chart cert-manager v1.21.3 (sha256:9ec67938b2981d8b333af61b3fcf53e26b4f6f5deb7ccda3de4ea116bb373a17). A CI test of the import proves the refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization builds and signs each bundle it approves with its own key, and imports only that bundle at its site.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: the offline bundle import accepts only what your organization signed.

statements.description: The offline bundle import accepts a bundle only when its manifest verifies with your organization's public key and refuses a bundle signed with any other key, so these items of Site certificate issuing reach the site only as your organization signed them: image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-controller v1.21.3@sha256:9b262e9493ab3e0daebc2c9cfbddc6df68b9ac91afc036a759584f3d49d607e5, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-webhook v1.21.3@sha256:fc2845cc042ab57c8b98c5ff62462d50dcd5d8d3302f9e6875cd05042ce1020b, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-cainjector v1.21.3@sha256:165691f631d61931a27e4fbbb82bbed8205431d0446b3c14d170081aeff75f0a, image quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-startupapicheck v1.21.3@sha256:6b9e17adc075c80c0c5cb1f901654f0efa4c5d4b1a8b369985ac67f5bbb0b8d2 and chart cert-manager v1.21.3 (sha256:9ec67938b2981d8b333af61b3fcf53e26b4f6f5deb7ccda3de4ea116bb373a17). A CI test of the import proves the refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization keeps the signing key, signs only the releases it approves, and keeps its own record of each bundle it imports.
